orgDesign.companyProfile: Netherlands-headquartered energy software and expertise-services group modeled on Eneve, with 28 years of experience counted from Energy21's founding in Utrecht in 1997 (as GEN; EBASE launched 2002 for BRP market messages). Vortex Capital Partners bought into Energy21 in 2022 and financed the add-ons: Ecedo (founded 2003, full SaaS platform 2013) and Jules (Loughborough, founded 2010/2011) joined in 2023, Gridhub (founded 2023) in 2024, and on 18 June 2025 Energy21, Ecedo, Jules and Gridhub became Eneve with 130+ specialists and an expected 2025 turnover of EUR 25M+. On 30 March 2026 Eneve acquired Nemon (Ascó, Catalonia; Nemon Trade Energy, Trade Energy CRM and Trade Energy SIPS; about 100 supplier customers in Spain and Portugal, roughly 30 specialists), taking the group to about 180 people across the Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, the UK and Paraguay and an expected turnover above EUR 30M. The platform serves 50+ energy companies (more than 100 energy suppliers including Iberia), processes 20 million connections daily, has its largest implementation at more than 25 million connections and validates over 90% of Dutch energy consumption data; named customers include Eneco, Essent, Engie, Vattenfall, Mega, Vandebron, Scholt Energie, Pure Energie, PZEM, EBN, Axpo, TotalEnergies, BASF, USG-Chemelot and Barcelona Energia. Revenue comes from software subscriptions per supplier or portfolio (scaling with connections, modules and MWh), BRP as a Service priced per MWh tier, implementation, market-entry and licensing projects, Eneve Academy training and support; the company generates, sells or trades no energy for its own account. Leadership: CEO Michiel Kuiper ("Our mission is to make the energy chain manageable and future-proof"), founder Gaston Hendriks, Teun Levering as Managing Director Software since June 2025, and Atilano Villanueva as Managing Director of Nemon alongside its founders Nàdia Contreras Jordà and Ivan Solé Martinez.
orgDesign.operatingModel: With about 180 people the organisation is built as five groups and fifteen teams of 5-14 people that own their bricks end to end (product, build, run, second-line support), each group led by a small working leadership rather than a management layer. The three suites map onto three product groups: the Supplier Suite Group (Ecedo and Gridhub heritage in the Netherlands, Nemon in Ascó) owns the Propose -> Onboard -> Bill -> Serve flow for suppliers in the Netherlands, Spain and Portugal; the Balancing and Shipping Group (Energy21 EBASE heritage; Utrecht) owns Measure -> Forecast -> Nominate -> Steer -> Settle and runs the engines behind BRP as a Service; the Trade and Portfolio Group (Jules heritage; Loughborough and Utrecht) owns Source and customer trading. The Market and Platform Group guards the two complicated subsystems the whole company depends on — Dutch and Iberian market communication and validated market data — and provides identity, tenant and brand isolation, workflow, migration tooling and the open API as platform services; part of its engineering capacity sits in Paraguay. The Expertise Services Group turns software into outcomes: a BRP-as-a-service operations desk that runs the guaranteed day-ahead, intraday (ETPA) and ex-post cycle for customer portfolios, market-entry scans and ACM/CNMC licensing support for new entrants, and implementation, heritage-product migration, Eneve Academy and support for every customer. Complicated-subsystem teams own market communication and meter data because a wrong message or a wrong allocation volume becomes a wrong bill, a wrong nomination and a compliance incident at once. Every team is steward of the data assets its bricks create, so the integrated market-operations data model — connection, contract, meter reading, allocation volume, nomination, trade, invoice and payment in one place across 20 million connections — remains the strategic asset, and the Vortex thesis of software plus services shows up as enabling teams that sell and operate what the product teams build.
